:::{#rem-matrix-induced-inner-product-bilinear}
#### A matrix-induced inner product is a symmetric bilinear form

When $\matr{A}$ is symmetric and positive definite (@def-positive-definite),
its matrix-induced inner product (@def-matrix-induced-inner-product)
equals its symmetric bilinear form (@def-symmetric-bilinear-form):

$$
\iprod{\vx}{\vy}_{\matr{A}} = \bform{\matr{A}}{\vx}{\vy}.
$$

A symmetric matrix that is not positive definite
still has a symmetric bilinear form,
but that form is not an inner product.
For example, take the symmetric matrix $\matr{B}$ of @exm-symmetric-bilinear-form
and the vector $\vecf{z} = \tp{(1, -1)}$:

$$
\ba
\bform{\matr{B}}{\vecf{z}}{\vecf{z}}
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(@def-bilinear-form)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 \cd 1 + 2 \cd (-1) \\ 2 \cd 1 + 1 \cd (-1) \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(multiply the matrix by } \vecf{z} \text{)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\\
&= 1 \cd (-1) + (-1) \cd 1
&& \text{(multiply the row by the column)}
\\
&= -2.
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

The quadratic form of $\matr{B}$ is negative at $\vecf{z}$,
so $\matr{B}$ is not positive definite (@def-positive-definite).

:::
